_comment: The single home for begehung's machine-read vocabularies and column
orders. SKILL.md explains what each value MEANS; this file is what the
values ARE, and tools/validate_begehung.py reads it rather than
restating it. A restated copy beside the parser it mirrors cannot age
loudly — the source gains a member and the copy stays green.
Drift between this file and SKILL.md is caught by the repo-owned check

roles._comment: Names WHICH member of an unordered vocabulary a check must single out by meaning. Without this the checker has to spell the value itself, which puts a second home for that value in the code. The checker reads the role; the schema owns the spelling.

required_rows._comment: `match` is the token a checker looks for in the axis cell to recognize the row. It lives here so a MAP written in another language, or with a house wording, changes ONE line instead of failing a faithful row — and so the checker branches on the schema rather than on its own copy.

cross_cutting.means: lifecycle row — where does it live, who writes it, who reads it

enforcer.means: the enforcer held to its own invariants (owed only where a surface emits verdicts about other work — a judgment the checker cannot make)
